title: NICHD lists reading to a child from birth as a way to help learning
summary: NICHD says caregivers can help by reading to a child, beginning when the child is born.
body: The NICHD page on promoting early learning says a caregiver can help by reading to the child, beginning when she or he is born. Reading sits in a short list with naming objects, listening and responding, and practicing counting. The page does not report a reading score or a required number of books. It presents the list as everyday opportunities, and it says home and daily life have a strong effect on learning. The page is a United States institute page.

sources.title: How can parents and caregivers promote early learning?
sources.author: Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Opened 2026-11-26. No updated date was printed on the page opened. Supports the bullet 'Reading to your child, beginning when she or he is born.'
